intent: Authenticated cardholder asks the bank to credit a second £900 today (on the strength of a merchant refund promise) and to close dispute DB-023 as won.
summary: Decline the second £900 credit and the request to close DB-023 as won: the ledger shows the £900 provisional credit PC-023 already booked and merchant refund total MR-023 at £0.00 as of 09:20, and the supplied disputes procedure requires reconciliation of a posted merchant refund before any adjustment; a merchant promise is not a posting event. Pass the merchant's refund email to the disputes team to record on DB-023 and monitor for posting. Reply to the customer with the recorded status, the reason, and what remains pending.

facts.claim: Authentication passed for Maren Folsey and the 09:15 chat is recorded as authenticated.
Dispute DB-023 is open with a provisional credit of £900.00 (reference PC-023).
The ledger shows the £900 card purchase (ORDER-023) booked 2026-10-30, the £900 dispute credit PC-023 provisional_booked 2026-11-05, and merchant_refund_total MR-023 at £0.00 as of 2026-11-11 09:20.

Cresswheel Furnishings emailed the customer agreeing to refund £900 for SYN-ORDER-023, expecting the card refund within three working days, with a processing reference to follow; no reference has been supplied.

The supplied disputes procedure states the disputes team reconciles any posted merchant refund against the provisional credit before authorising an adjustment, and that a merchant promise alone is not a posting event.
The customer asks for another £900 to be added today and for the dispute to be closed as won, saying any later merchant payment can be sorted afterwards.
No desk response to the final request is recorded.

missing: Merchant processing reference for the promised refund (merchant said it will follow).
Whether and when the merchant refund actually posts to SYN-ACCT-B023 (MR-023 total is £0.00 as of 09:20).
Disputes team's final determination on DB-023 after reconciliation.

steps.instruction: Decline the request in E05 to add a further £900 to SYN-ACCT-B023 today and to close DB-023 as won. Reason: provisional credit PC-023 (£900) is already provisional_booked; merchant_refund_total MR-023 is £0.00 as of 2026-11-11 09:20; the supplied disputes procedure requires the disputes team to reconcile a posted merchant refund against the provisional credit before authorising any adjustment, and a merchant promise is not a posting event. Leave PC-023 in place and DB-023 open; make no ledger change.

rationale.explanation: A second £900 would duplicate the provisional credit already booked for the same £900 purchase, and no merchant refund has posted to reconcile against. Closing as won is a disputes-team determination, not a customer-directed action.
rationale.criterion: A refund promise is not a booked credit; adjustments to a provisional credit follow reconciliation of a posted merchant refund per the supplied disputes procedure.

steps.instruction: Send the Brackenfold Bank disputes team a note for DB-023: attach the merchant email of 2026-11-11 09:10 from Cresswheel Furnishings agreeing to refund £900 for SYN-ORDER-023 (processing reference not yet supplied); state that MR-023 shows £0.00 as of 09:20 and PC-023 remains provisional; ask them to record the merchant's promise on the file, monitor for the merchant refund posting, and reconcile per their procedure. State explicitly that no adjustment or second credit is authorised by the desk and the customer's request for an additional £900 has been declined.

rationale.explanation: The merchant's agreement to refund is material to the dispute's reconciliation and should sit with the team that owns the reconciliation step, without the desk pre-empting the outcome.
rationale.criterion: Disputes team reconciles any posted merchant refund against the provisional credit before authorising an adjustment.

steps.instruction: Reply to Maren Folsey in the chat: 'Thank you for sending the shop's email. Our records show the £900 provisional credit (PC-023) is already on your account while dispute DB-023 stays open. As of 09:20 today no refund from Cresswheel Furnishings has posted to your account, so the shop's message is a promise to refund, not a payment received. We can't add a second £900 now: that would give you the £900 twice for the same purchase, and our disputes team reconciles any merchant refund that actually posts against the provisional credit before making any adjustment. We also can't close the dispute as won at the desk; the disputes team decides the outcome once reconciliation is done. I am passing the shop's email to the disputes team to note on DB-023 (this is pending their acknowledgement). If the shop sends you the processing reference, please send it to us and we will add it to the file. The three-working-day timing is the shop's expectation, not something we can confirm.' Do not state any further credit or closure outcome.

rationale.explanation: The customer needs the recorded ledger and dispute status, the reason the second credit is declined, and what remains pending, without promises about the merchant refund or dispute outcome.
rationale.criterion: State only the stage the supplied record proves; a refund promise is not proof of a posted credit and no arrival time is promised absent an applicable commitment.

must_state: The £900 provisional credit PC-023 is already on the account while DB-023 is open.
No merchant refund has posted to the account as of 11 November 09:20 (MR-023 total £0.00); the merchant's email is a promise, not a posting.

The bank will not add a second £900 now because that would duplicate the provisional credit already given; the disputes team reconciles any posted merchant refund against the provisional credit before any adjustment.
The desk cannot close DB-023 as won on request; the outcome is determined by the disputes team.
The merchant's email has been passed to the disputes team to record on DB-023 (pending acknowledgement) and the customer can send the merchant's processing reference when received.
must_not: Do not promise or imply a second £900 credit will be added today or later.
Do not state the dispute is closed, won or resolved.
Do not claim the merchant refund has been received or will arrive within three working days; that timing is the merchant's expectation, not a bank commitment.
Do not describe the provisional credit as final or permanent.
Do not claim the disputes team has already recorded or acted on the merchant email; that forwarding is pending execution.
